messages:
alex: Heads-up — CS flagged several customers getting 429s but the Console quota panels show 0 usage / full allowance. Customers all using service-type API keys. Samples below, can someone take a quick look?

cs-eli: customer IDs: cust-889, cust-902, cust-914. Started ~2026-03-11 22:10 UTC, intermittent spikes of 429s. They sent request IDs as well.

alex: paste of enforcer log snippet:
```
2026-03-11T22:12:03Z enforcer[prod-12] INFO req=req_0a1b2c action=check result=throttled key=svc_abc tenant_id= -- owner_id=org-889 token_role=service
2026-03-11T22:12:03Z enforcer[prod-12] INFO req=req_0a1b2d action=check result=throttled key=svc_def tenant_id= -- owner_id=org-902 token_role=service
```

matt: interesting — enforcer shows owner_id populated but tenant_id is `--`. Console panels and our aggregation queries still group by tenant_id. If the producer switched tags, aggregated metrics might be empty while raw enforcer logs show hits. :eyes:

priya: I can confirm from ingest logs: the metric producer deployed on 2026-03-11 renamed the label `tenant_id` -> `owner_id` in the event payload. Ingest service wrote raw rows, but the materialized views used by the dashboard still expect tenant_id.

ingest-bot: new-metrics: wrote 1240 rows with owner_id populated and tenant_id NULL for index=rate_hits_prod between 2026-03-11T21:55:00Z and 2026-03-12T02:00:00Z

matt: reproduction query to see orphaned counts (ClickHouse):
```
SELECT owner_id, count() FROM rate_hits_prod WHERE owner_id IS NOT NULL AND tenant_id IS NULL AND ts >= '2026-03-11' GROUP BY owner_id ORDER BY count() DESC LIMIT 20;
```

alex: ran that and got the 3 affected customers at top — matches CS list. So panels return 0 because they read materialized view `mv_rate_hourly_by_tenant`.

lucy: customer impact: 7 customers total, mostly enterprise and service keys. Reporting window since deploy; billing unaffected but monitoring/alerting misleads customer support and customers see inconsistent UI vs actual throttling. This is causing escalations. :bug:

priya: short-term mitigation: update the dashboard queries to coalesce(owner_id, tenant_id) so both tag names are accepted. I can push a Query-as-Code change for the Console dashboards — low risk. Then run a backfill to populate materialized views for the last 7 days.

matt: longer-term: revert producer change or make producer write both labels for 48h during transition. We'll also add a schema contract enforcement in the producer CI so label name changes require a migration plan.

alex: proposed immediate action items:
- priya: hotfix dashboard queries to use coalesce(owner_id, tenant_id) (ETA 30m)
- priya/matt: kick backfill job for mv_rate_hourly_by_tenant for 7 days (ETA 2h to start, may take longer)
- matt: patch producer to write tenant_id as duplicate label for compatibility (ETA 4h)
- lucy: notify CS + customers with a short note that UI counts temporary mismatch, monitoring/enforcement was correct (I'll draft)

quota-bot: alert-suppression: created temporary alert rule silence for rate-panel-mismatch until 2026-03-12T06:00:00Z to avoid noisy pages.

priya: hotfix deployed to Console dashboards — queries now use `coalesce(owner_id, tenant_id)` and temp panel shows expected counts. Backfill job submitted (job id backfill-1976) starting now.

matt: started producer compatibility patch to emit both labels and added a unit test to assert both keys in the outgoing event. Pushed to release branch.

alex: thanks. lucy can you coordinate CS comms? Also open a postmortem ticket and mark severity P2 for now.

lucy: will send a customer note in 20m and open a postmortem ticket (PM-1234). Draft: "We observed a mismatch between enforcement logs and Console quota panels caused by a labeling change during a recent deploy. Throttling behavior was correct; the UI aggregation missed the new label. We're fixing the dashboard and backfilling metrics"

cs-eli: customer replies already calm down once we told them enforcement was accurate. They appreciate the transparency.

priya: backfill job progress: 10% complete after 18 minutes. No errors so far. I'll update when done.

matt: note for follow-up: add an integration test that deploys a dummy producer with altered labels and asserts Console panels reflect counts within 5 minutes. Prevents silent label drift in future.

alex: closing loop here — will update thread when backfill completes and when producer patch is live. Great triage, team. :thumbsup:
